samples.summary: Vacuous assertion in the "remembered heading level is inert" suite: the plain-text test cannot fail
samples.evidence: `test('plain-text serialization is unaffected')` asserts `expect(serializeText({ blocks: [bulletedHeading] })).toContain('Quarterly results')`. `packages/docs/src/serialize/text.ts:60-71` (`blockToText`) switches only on `horizontal-rule` / `page-break` / `table` and otherwise emits the inline text — it never reads `block.type === 'heading'` or `headingLevel`. The assertion therefore holds for a heading, a list item, a paragraph, and would hold even if the heading-memory invariant were completely broken. It is presented as one of four guards of the invariant but contributes no coverage.

samples.summary: New exported predicate `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` has no direct unit test; only two happy-path integration paths exercise it
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/test/store/block-helpers.test.ts:405-430` (`describe('applyMergeBlocks')`) was not touched by this delta and contains no case with `headingLevel`. The only coverage is via `Doc.deleteBackward` in list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts (one drop case, one keep case) and the two Yorkie tests. Untested branches of the predicate: a `heading`-typed block with empty inlines (must NOT drop), a `list-item` with no `headingLevel`, a `list-item` with `inlines: []`, and a `list-item` whose inlines are all empty strings across several inline nodes.

samples.evidence: Both new tests (packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:1207-1255) build two top-level body blocks via `store.setDocument`, so `blockPath` has length 1 and `endPath = [idx+1]`. `mergeBlock` is region- and table-aware (`resolveBlockTreePath`, `getBlocksArrayForPath`) and existing tests merge inside a table cell (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:1709) and in header/footer regions, but no test merges an emptied bulleted heading in a table cell or header, so the `[...blockPath] with last segment +1` range used for `removeStyleByPath` on a nested path is unexercised.

samples.evidence: The test dispatches the shortcut twice and only asserts the final block is still `paragraph` with no `headingLevel` — exactly the input state. finding.summary: TextEditor.toggleList's new heading-restoring exit has no test at all
finding.evidence: The diff changes three toggleList implementations and the new test file only exercises one of them (`initialize`/EditorAPI in packages/docs/test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:192-249). `TextEditor.toggleList` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2164-2172) is private and only reachable via the Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+7 / +8 shortcuts (text-editor.ts:957-968); I found no test that dispatches those keys or otherwise reaches it. The stated purpose of `unlistedBlockType` is to keep these three implementations from drifting, yet two of the three call sites can regress (e.g. reverting to hardcoded 'paragraph') with the suite still green.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no test reaches the private TextEditor.toggleList heading-restoring exit via the Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+7/8 shortcuts. The same new test file contains describe('keyboard bullet shortcut round trip') (list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:330-396) whose pressListShortcut helper (lines 340-355) dispatches a real keydown with key '7'/'8' plus ctrlKey+metaKey+shiftKey on the textarea that TextEditor itself mounts and listens on (text-editor.ts:419,428,431; constructed by initialize at editor.ts:2084). mod resolves from metaKey/ctrlKey (text-editor.ts:728) and both are set, so the event reaches case '7'/'8' -> this.toggleList (text-editor.ts:957-968) -> the private implementation at text-editor.ts:2164-2180. Assertions are non-vacuous and fail if the exit reverts to hardcoded 'paragraph': after one press block must be list-item with headingLevel preserved (lines 362-363, which also proves the key path was actually handled), after the second press it must be heading with level 2/3 (lines 367-368, 380-381), plus a paragraph negative control (385-395). The reviewer's greps missed it because the key is '7'/'8' (not 'Digit7') produced by a ternary and the shortcut is invoked through a helper rather than by naming toggleList. The file runs under the package's `vitest --run` script with default test/**/*.test.ts include and a jsdom environment/canvas shim.

finding.summary: The new 'headingLevel is inert on a list-item' invariant is asserted in a comment but nothing tests it (export/serialize/clipboard readers)
finding.evidence: The change introduces a genuinely new document state — a `list-item` block that carries `headingLevel` — and the `Block` doc comment claims 'every reader (export, `blockStyleId`, toolbar labels) gates on `type === 'heading'`'. No test in the diff or the suite feeds such a block to any reader. I checked markdown serialization (src/serialize/markdown.ts:103), pdf outline (src/export/pdf-exporter.ts:201), docx export (src/export/docx-exporter.ts:184), `blockStyleId` (src/model/named-styles.ts:99) and clipboard copy (`cloneBlockWithFreshIds`, text-editor.ts:3404, which copies `headingLevel` verbatim, plus paste head/tail merges at text-editor.ts:3578/3607). The new tests assert only `type`/`headingLevel` fields on the store and Doc; if any of those readers stopped gating on type, or a copied bulleted heading pasted into body text resurrected as a heading, every test in this diff would still pass.

verdict.reason: The finding's central claim — "No test in the diff or the suite feeds such a block to any reader" — is false. packages/docs/test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:398-431 is a dedicated describe block ("a remembered heading level is inert while the block is a list item") whose doc comment states its purpose: "Assert the invariant instead of trusting the comment." It builds exactly the disputed state (lines 404-412: type 'list-item', listKind 'unordered', headingLevel 2) and feeds it to four readers, three of which the finding named by file:line: serializeMarkdown (:415 expects '- Quarterly results', guarding markdown.ts:103), blockStyleId (:419 expects 'normal', guarding named-styles.ts:105), serializeText (:423), and DOCX export (:429 expects the XML NOT to contain 'w:pStyle w:val="Heading'). The assertions are non-vacuous: I read the readers and each gate is the thing under test — named-styles.ts:105 switches on block.type, and docx-exporter.ts:184 does (block.type === 'heading' ? block.headingLevel : undefined), feeding docx-style-map.ts:96 which emits a pStyle val of Heading+level. Removing any gate flips a test red. The DOCX negative assertion is paired with a positive toContain('Quarterly results') at :428, so it cannot pass on an empty export. The file runs under the default vitest include (packages/docs/vite.config.ts declares no restricting include). The same file also covers the merge-drops-stale-memory path (:217-261) and both toggleList implementations. Residual: PDF outline (pdf-exporter.ts:196 addOutlineFromHeadings) and clipboard paste are not fed this state, but that is a breadth gap on a core behavior that IS tested — minor under this rubric, not the claimed major "no meaningful test at all".
